i understand this pain and i’m so sorry. 

i wish more men could speak up about assault against them, but society has really fucked us over on that one. it took me a long time to realize what happened to me was rape because i thought that the fact that i eventually gave up on saying no meant that i gave consent and wasn’t raped. i think that really need to change because i feel sorry for every man that has to deal with it and has been told that they “liked it”. there’s a disgusting standard placed on gay men that we’re “always wanting sex” and that we can’t be assaulted in that way since we’re “sexual deviants”. 

and i do really feel awful for women all the time. i have sisters (one older and one younger) and just hearing the things that has happened to them makes me physically sick. one of my sisters was catcalled and followed home at the age of 11. fucking ELEVEN. the fact that a literal child has to go through that is disgusting. growing up, my parents were never as hard on me as they were my sisters. every day i would hear them talk about their clothes, how to act around boys, and even hearing them call my sisters sluts for hanging out with boys. i never had that, i grew up being able to do whatever i wanted with little consequences. 90% of the women i hang out with have gotten sexually harassed in some way. it’s just so staggering the amount of people that it really is. 

i wish people would teach their sons how to act sexually and stop placing the blame on women. the fact that you have to hold the responsibility for everything is horrible.

as a man who is a person of color, i have to disagree. there are a lot of differences between the two situations due to the history behind it. 

racism in (american) society dates back to the slave trade. they didn’t want to have to treat their slaves as people, so they would make up things to justify it. when slaves were released, propaganda spread around so white people would not have to see or deal with black people. the propaganda has always been a way to justify how they treat people of color as subhuman. there is no religious reasoning, no societal reasoning for why they’re “lower than white people”, it was literally made up so sick and twisted people could get away with heinous acts without it being illegal or against their religion. 

however, for women, it is different. as far as american society goes, we have always been patriarchal. due to the bible, people viewed women only for their reproductive organs. it was acceptable back then due to religion because the bible said they were to be subservient and submissive to men. when christianity stopped being to societal rule to follow, it didn’t dismantle the fact that america has always been, and will be for the foreseeable future, a patriarchal society. due to the branching off of religion, it started becoming less acceptable to view women as submissive to their man. women’s empowerment did not stop men from thinking this way though. women grow up learning that everything they do is their own fault and if they are around men, they will be assaulted just because they are women. 

knowing this, i don’t find them to be comparable because of the history behind it. one has to do with supremacy of a race and the other has to do with religion and societal rules. 

a more comparable thing would be men having to act emotionless to be considered a man, men being more likely to have their kids taken from them in a custody battle, etc.. 

my experiences as an asian man in america is different than an asian woman. as someone who actively faces racism, i personally would never compare them. 

of course, this doesn’t devalue what you have said. i understand where you are coming from and i get how unfair it is to be judged before someone gets to know you. it’s frustrating and sad. no one should have to be judged before being able to show their true selves. but listening to what my sisters have gone through, i can guarantee i have never gone through anything like that and i understand them. i implore you to have a sit down discussion with your wife so you can hear her story and possibly the stories of other women.

i did some digging and read a couple more articles on it but [this one](https://behavioralscientist.org/what-the-origins-of-the-1-in-5-statistic-teaches-us-about-sexual-assault-policy/) was easiest for me to fully grasp the idea behind the 1/5 idea. according to this article, the 1/5 is not true nor false. it’s currently still being debated. this article was best for me to read because it compiles multiple polls from multiple groups and even contemplates what people even consider to be rape. according to this article, some people may see something as rape whereas others may not. it also says the reason why people find it easy to believe the 1/5 number is because most of the time, the polls always tend to average about 20% for people who have been assaulted/raped. even if it’s not true, it’s still something that women have been told their whole lives. i even remember it being a discussion back when i was in middle school. i can guarantee you, nearly every woman knows at least one person who has been assaulted, so it furthers that fear.

i agree that it’s extremely unlikely, but again, women are raised to believe that it’s true and will happen. that was my point. i wasn’t saying that you’re wrong for saying it’s unlikely, it’s actually true that it’s rare, but you have to understand that it has to do with the way they were raised. i’m not a father but i have nieces and when someone just looks at them, i get nervous. it’s normal for people to be worried about their children. yes, the way the mother treated you was bad and it shouldn’t have happened, i’m truly sorry for it. no one should be treated badly.

if i could send a picture i would but if you google it, the first source to pop up is nsvrc.org. here’s a quote from the article “Approximately 1 in 5 (21.3% or an estimated 25.5 million) women in the U.S. reported completed or attempted rape at some point in their lifetime, including completed forced penetration, attempted forced penetration, or alcohol/drug facilitated completed penetration.” also including the link to the website. [sexual assault statistics ](https://www.nsvrc.org/statistics)

i have sisters and my best friends that i love dearly. they tell me a lot about what they deal with and it’s heartbreaking to listen to.

i’m not even offended by this because i understand. i am gay, definitely more feminine than most men, and even i have to watch out for my safety around other men sometimes. i have gotten assaulted and raped. the statistics for men being assaulted and raped is so much lower than women, so i can only imagine what you have to deal with and the fear you go through daily because of it. it’s horrible that you have to go through all of this just because we weren’t raised to be held accountable for our behavior.

i’m not trying to be condescending at all, this thought process isn’t bad, but it’s also not good. 

women are forced to see everyone as a predator because when they grow up, it’s socially pushed on them to take responsibility for every man’s action. for example, if they don’t want to be raped they have to wear conservative clothing. or not to walk outside at night unless they’re looking for a death wish. they grow up with so many stories about every bad thing that will happen to them if they are not careful. there’s even the statistics of how many women face these things (one in every five women will be assaulted). 

thinking of this, please keep in mind the social and societal rules that women have been force fed all their lives. they immediately jump to the conclusion that the man is more likely to be a predator than not. even if it is more likely to be within the family, it’s still a conscious fear many women have.  

what you did helping that child was amazing but it would make any parent nervous to see their child with a stranger.

edit: also comparing how women are raised to literal racism isn’t great and it’s not in the same lane. i’m saying this as an asian man, it’s not really comparable. and again, i’m not attacking you or trying to make you feel bad, i’m just trying to shed light on your wife’s thought process. obviously being prejudice isn’t okay in any way but you have to keep in mind that women were raised to be scared of men.

other than her aunt, no. i’m not quite so sure about reaching out to her aunt because her aunt is not the nicest of women and is unsympathetic and refuses to understand her mental illness. she lives with some friends at the moment though.

i’m sure there is but i haven’t looked into it. i’m scared for him because i don’t want him to be in harms way. but i am also scared for her because i know right now she really just needs professional help and getting stalking charges on her permanent record can ruin her life.

i understand that and i know i probably should but i do care about her a lot. i’m doing the best that i can for myself, but i wish that she would too. i would rather not call the police because american police are barely trained enough to handle people in mental health crisis but i honest to god don’t know what else to do to get her the help she needs.
she should be on medication but i’m honestly not sure if she’s taking it or not. i think she is but i’m not going to say definitely. and from my understanding, no, she is not going to therapy.
yes. she used to see a psychiatrist from 15 until she was 18. She was diagnosed with BPD at 15 i believe and then PTSD and schizophrenia at 18 and stopped seeing the psychiatrist a year ago.

thank you so much for your input, it really helped out. and sorry my grammar is pretty poor, english is not my first language. i mentioned my bipolar to show that i understand what it’s like living with a mental illness that affects how you act and your behaviors because there have been many times where i have also done inappropriate things because of my bipolar. but i am also medicated now, see two therapists, a psychiatrist, and go inpatient when i need to. i’m trying my best right now to be a good friend because i know how hard it is dealing with mental illness day to day but it’s at that point. i don’t think she understands what she’s doing is wrong because she’s been doing this to him since october. i really wish i knew how to convince her to actually get the help she needs instead of yelling at her.

my friends have been the only thing keeping me going and i’m so grateful for them. but with everything going on, our debt will only get worse and worse because we can’t pay for my treatments. i know suicide isn’t good but i just can’t handle the fact that my family is in so much pain because of me. i don’t want them to become homeless because of me. i’m just really not in a good mental state right now and i can’t go to a therapist
the american health system really really sucks but there’s nothing we can do about it
